newsitem.title: NEPAL: South Asia trade negotiators begin talks in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: South Asia trade negotiators begin talks in Nepal.

text.p: Diplomats from seven South Asian nations began talks in Nepal on Tuesday on cutting tariffs to bolster trade among developing countries in the region, officials said.

They said the three-day talks of the South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) aimed to enlarge the list of products on which tariffs would be reduced to about 3,000 items from more than 1,800 items now.

"The third round of SAPTA negotiations is expected to enlarge the schedules of concession ... and is expected to become another important milestone on the path of liberalising intra-regional trade fully," the Kathmandu-based South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) secretariat said in a statement.
In the first and second rounds of SAPTA negotiations ended last November, more than 1,800 products were identified for tariff concessions ranging from 10 percent to 100 percent.
The officials said the talks also aimed to deepen existing tariff cuts to boost regional trade, which represents only 3.4 percent of total global trade.
SAARC diplomats said the negotiations would be a major step towards launching a South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) by 2001.

SAARC, which groups Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, was formed in December 1985 to improve the economies of the seven developing nations, which together comprise more than one-fifth of the world's population.
Negotiators said bilateral talks during earlier rounds of SAPTA negotiations had been slow because they focused on specific products one at a time.
They said the latest talks will consider products according to their sectors and across the board to speed up the process.
